# Authoring HTML pages (the "HTML pages" visual tier)

Each `html` scene is one designed full-screen page (1920×1080) you author at
`<out_dir>/pages/scene_NN.html`, rendered by headless Chrome. The page is screenshotted at
progress `p=0..1`; `seek.js` freezes its CSS reveals so the entrance animates then holds.

## Boilerplate (link the bundled design system)
```html
<!doctype html><html><head><meta charset="utf-8">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/base.css">
<!-- theme.css lives at <out_dir>/theme.css — generated by scripts/theme.py, NOT in the skill assets dir -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/theme.css">
<!-- motifs.css is in the skill assets dir -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/motifs.css">
<!-- 9:16 ONLY: link the shipped vertical override LAST (see "9:16 vertical pages") -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/vertical.css">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="stage"><!-- your layout --></div>
  <script src="file:///ABS/PATH/TO/skill/assets/html/seek.js"></script>
</body></html>
```
Use absolute `file://` paths. Order: `base.css` → `theme.css` (from `<out_dir>`) → `motifs.css` → **(9:16 only) `vertical.css`** (all from `assets/html/`). On a 16:9 deck, DROP the `vertical.css` line.
**Register-contest candidate pages (SKILL.md 3.55) substitute the theme link:** they link their OWN
`<out_dir>/_contest/<key>/theme.css` instead — `<out_dir>/theme.css` doesn't exist yet at contest time.

## Form selection — choose the form the CONTENT wants (do NOT default to a card grid)
**Design is choosing, not matching.** A `.card`/`.row` grid is the right answer ONLY for **parallel,
unordered, equal-weight** items. The moment the content has **order, magnitude, a relationship, time,
or two axes**, a non-card form says it better. For each beat, name the 2–3 forms it *could* take, then
pick the one whose shape matches the content (all classes are in `base.css`, all reveal-ready):

| The content is… | Reach for |
|---|---|
| **A few standout numbers / KPIs** | `.scorecard` (3 `.tile`: big `.num` + `.lab`, optional `.delta up/down`) — or one hero `.stat` + `.unit` when a single number IS the point |
| **A process / sequence / steps** | `.flow` (`.step` = `.n`/`.t`/`.s`, `.arrow` between; mark a focal/constraint step `.step.on`, `--focal:var(--accent2)` for a risk step) — or `.timeline` if the steps are dated or one is the focus (`.tl-node.on`) |
| **A relationship / structure** (inputs→decision, centre+peers) | `.hubspoke` (`.hs-spoke` × N → `.hs-connect` → `.hs-hub`) |
| **Two axes / a positioning** | `.quadrant` (2×2 `.cell`, focal `.cell.on`, `.ax-x`/`.ax-y` labels) |
| **Parts of a whole / a share** | `.segbar` (100% stacked `.seg`, widths inline) or `.meter` (`.fill` width inline) |
| **Visible surface vs hidden bulk** (submerged cost/complexity/work — "what you see is a fraction") | `.iceberg` — a small `.tip` above the `.waterline`, 2–4 `.ib-point` in the `.mass` below (motion-native: pan DOWN past the waterline uncovers the mass; see `motion-grammar.md`). NOT three parallel cards |
| **A comparison** (A vs B, before→after) | a two-column split — `.split` (full-page) or an inline `grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr` of two `.reveal-up` wrappers each holding a `.card` / `.card defocus` (defocus the non-focal side); see the `before_after` template. `.quadrant` if two real axes |
| **One idea / a verbatim line** | `.pullquote` (+ `<cite>`) — or a single hero `.stat` |
| **Colour-coded categories** (bold, scannable) | `.blocks two` / `.blocks three` — one hue per `.block` from the THEME: `var(--accent)`, `var(--accent2)`, and for a 3rd either `var(--green)` (a theme-neutral alias) or a `color-mix(in srgb,var(--accent) 55%,var(--accent2))`; verify the 3rd doesn't clash — if you need 3 strongly-distinct on-brand hues and the theme only has 2, use `.blocks two` or `cards` instead. Never grey filler, never a raw hex. |
| **A decomposition** (165 = 123 + 42) | a `.grid` of labeled `.bar` rows (widths inline) or a `.segbar` |
| **Truly parallel, equal-weight items** | a `.card` grid (`.dash` 3-up / `.grid-asym`) — the *considered* choice for THIS shape only |
| **A title / section** | `.kicker` + `.rule` + `.title` (+ `.sub`); a mono `.chrome` footer ties the deck together — ONLY when `meta.captions:false` (see `.chrome` note below) |

For each beat, record the pick as a one-line **form ledger**: *winner — beats `<runner-up>` because …*
(the design-director emits this; the design-critic audits it).

**Premium templates — don't reinvent the composition.** For the richer composite forms, start from a
verified, ready-to-adapt page in **`references/html-templates.md`** (`hero_stat`, `before_after`,
`timeline_rail`, `problem_leak`/funnel, `system_map`, `metric_wall` = dashboard-with-one-hero-metric,
`case_story`, `flywheel`) — copy it, swap in your REAL content, keep the reveals + cues. These are quality
floors to ADAPT, not fixed slots; the plain archetype snippets above are for simpler beats.

## Reveal animation (so the page captures cleanly)
- Add `class="reveal"` or `class="reveal-up"` to elements you want to animate in.
- Stagger by giving later elements an inline positive delay: `style="animation-delay:.18s"`.
- ONLY use CSS animations via these classes. **No** `setTimeout`/JS-driven motion, **no** external
  network assets (images/fonts/CDNs) — they break deterministic, offline, seekable capture.
- ⚠️ **NEVER put an inline `opacity` on a reveal element.** The reveal classes hide the element via
  `opacity:0` in the CLASS; an inline `opacity:.92` overrides that, so the element is VISIBLE before
  its cue/delay ever fires (content leads the voice — it shipped as a real bug). To dim a reveal
  element, put the transparency in the COLOR instead:
  `color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--on-accent) 92%,transparent)`.

## Faithfulness (required)
Every number, name, date, and claim on the page must come from the material (or a verified
source) — type the real data into the HTML. Never invent figures or labels. Data lives on the
page as real text/bars, not as a decorative picture. The critic checks the page against the
narration (R2 audio↔visual) and the facts (R1d/R1e).

## Example (a faithful breakdown page)
```html
<div class="stage">
  <div class="kicker reveal">2025 · 165 次发射</div>
  <div class="rule reveal" style="animation-delay:.05s"></div>
  <div class="title reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.1s">真正能争夺的，只有一小块</div>
  <div class="grid" style="margin-top:40px">
    <div class="bar reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.25s;width:74%;background:var(--blue)">自用 Starlink · 123</div>
    <div class="bar reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.4s;width:26%;background:var(--orange)">对外发射 · 42</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Motifs & pictures (make pages fancier)

Also link `assets/html/motifs.css` (after `base.css`). Motifs are **atmosphere behind real
content** — they assert no fact, so they stay decorative; the real data is the text/bars.

**CSS motifs** — put backdrops as direct children of `<body>`, BEFORE `.stage` (content sits above):
- `<div class="bg-stars"></div>` — a deterministic starfield.
- `<div class="bg-glow blue" style="width:640px;height:640px;top:-120px;right:-120px"></div>` — a soft accent glow (position + size inline).
- `<div class="ghost">165</div>` — an oversized faint number behind the content.
- `<span class="grad-text">…</span>` — gradient accent text.
- Motion (seekable, paused): `class="float"` — a slow one-shot upward drift from +26px to rest
  (NOT a loop/bob); distinct from `class="reveal-up"` which is a 48px entrance + fade. Use `.float`
  for atmospheric elements that settle into position; use `.reveal-up` for content entrances.

**Stroke weight for video:** information-carrying SVG/diagram strokes are **≥2px** — thin lines
die under yuv420p encoding. The 1px `--hairline` card border is decorative only (cards are
delineated by surface + shadow); never use a 1px stroke to carry meaning.

**Inline SVG motifs** (copy-paste; style with `fill`/`stroke`/`.float`/`.draw`):
```html
<!-- generic rocket silhouette -->
<svg width="180" height="320" viewBox="0 0 60 120" class="float" style="position:absolute;right:160px;top:300px;z-index:1">
  <path d="M30 4 C42 22 44 52 44 78 H16 C16 52 18 22 30 4 Z" fill="var(--blue)"/>
  <path d="M16 78 L4 104 L18 92 Z M44 78 L56 104 L42 92 Z" fill="var(--orange)"/>
  <circle cx="30" cy="46" r="7" fill="var(--bg)"/>
</svg>
<!-- orbit ring (use .draw for a stroke-on; path/circle must set pathLength="1") -->
<svg width="520" height="520" viewBox="0 0 200 200" style="position:absolute;left:-80px;bottom:-120px;z-index:1;opacity:.5">
  <circle cx="100" cy="100" r="90" fill="none" stroke="var(--surface)" stroke-width="2" pathLength="1" class="draw"/>
</svg>
```

### Topical motif backdrop — the free way to make a flat page look fancier *and* on-topic
In the **flat/free tier** (no AI images) a content page defaults to a bare `--bg` — clean, but flat,
and generic decoration (`.bg-stars`/`.bg-glow`) doesn't *say* anything about the subject. Instead,
draw a **simple diagram derived from THIS deck's `motif`** (the recurring atmosphere idea — NOT the
`signature_concept`, which must carry its meaning in the FOREGROUND) and place it FAINT behind the
content — the programmatic cousin of the AI `.bg-soft`: free, deterministic, and *about the topic*.
It's the flat-mode answer to "background flatness" and freshens covers + main pages.

Rules (same faithfulness contract as any motif): it stays a **whisper** (content pages `opacity
~.06–.12`, a flat-mode hero/cover `~.14–.22`) and asserts **no DATA** — no real number/label AND no
real trend, proportion, rank, or magnitude may be reproduced in the backdrop, even without labels
(a ghosted *shape* a viewer could read as its own data point is a faithfulness break). Add a
`.bg-soft-tint` after it **only where text actually overlaps the motif** — a full-bleed tint lays
38–70 % of `--bg` over everything below it, so tinting a motif that sits in empty space (text on the
opposite side) just washes the already-faint motif out; when text and motif share a zone, raise the
motif toward the hero band or scrim just behind the text instead. Use `.bg-motif` (a full-bleed
container; its `currentColor` is `var(--muted)` — override `color:var(--accent)` inline) or the
ready-made `.bg-grid` schematic. Put it as the FIRST child of `<body>`. On a **9:16** deck, compose
the motif around the vertical centre (a landscape-anchored motif is cropped away) — see "9:16".

```html
<!-- A) ready-made schematic grid — any system/engineering/plan topic (mask fades it at the edges) -->
<div class="bg-grid" style="--cell:80px"></div><div class="bg-soft-tint"></div>

<!-- B) ghosted node-network — an AI/agents/systems deck (echo the page's real "5 seats → agents").
     NO .bg-soft-tint here: text sits on the LEFT, the network on the RIGHT — they don't overlap, so a
     tint would only wash the motif out. `meet` (not `slice`) so the network still fits on a 9:16 crop. -->
<div class="bg-motif" style="opacity:.10;color:var(--accent)"><svg viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <g fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
    <line x1="1360" y1="240" x2="1600" y2="440"/><line x1="1600" y1="440" x2="1430" y2="700"/>
    <line x1="1430" y1="700" x2="1180" y2="620"/><line x1="1180" y1="620" x2="1360" y2="240"/>
    <line x1="1600" y1="440" x2="1180" y2="620"/></g>
  <g fill="currentColor">
    <circle cx="1360" cy="240" r="9"/><circle cx="1600" cy="440" r="9"/>
    <circle cx="1430" cy="700" r="9"/><circle cx="1180" cy="620" r="9"/></g>
</svg></div>

<!-- C) faint segmented bar — an 80/20 (or any share) deck; echoes the split's SHAPE, no numbers.
     The band spans the centre where text sits, so a .bg-soft-tint is warranted. -->
<div class="bg-motif" style="opacity:.10"><svg viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="none">
  <rect x="0" y="470" width="1536" height="140" fill="currentColor"/>
  <rect x="1536" y="470" width="384" height="140" fill="var(--accent)" opacity=".6"/>
</svg></div><div class="bg-soft-tint"></div>
```
A strong variant is a **whisper of the beat's OWN shape** — but *redraw a simplified SVG echo* of it,
don't lift the live element: most archetypes (flow/roster/timeline/quadrant) are CSS/DIV with no SVG
to take, and a real chart's SVG carries `data-cue-index`/`data-cue`/`id`/`.reveal*` that would poison
reveal timing if copied in. **The backdrop must be INERT** — strip every cue/id/reveal marker
(`validate.py` flags any that remain inside a backdrop). Echo only STRUCTURE (a flow's topology, a
roster's arrangement), never a real data shape; put the echo on a DIFFERENT beat (or the hero), never
behind the very chart it mirrors; keep it toward `--muted` so foreground data and background
atmosphere never blur. Keep ONE motif family recurring across a FEW beats (a system, not clip-art or a
wallpaper on every page — other beats still rotate plain/tinted/accent-fill).

**Pictures (`gpt-image` backdrops or your own photos)** — a LOCAL image is allowed (a `file://`
path is offline/deterministic; only NETWORK assets are forbidden). Use it as a darkened backdrop:
```html
<img class="bg-photo" src="file:///ABS/PATH/assets/bg_01.png" alt="">
<div class="scrim"></div>
<div class="stage"><!-- legible text over the photo --></div>
```
A gpt-image backdrop must stay **generic/atmospheric** (`broll`) — no fabricated specific
vehicle/event/figure, no embedded numbers — the facts live in the page text, never in the image.

## Documentary (REAL) images — the SCRAPED, license-clean tier
For a **concrete** subject (a place, landmark, real object/device/organism, a real map/diagram, a
historical scene), a REAL image DEMONSTRATES the point far better than generated atmosphere — and it's
faithful because it's the real, sourced thing. The design-director marks such beats
`media.treatment:"documentary"` (see its "IMAGERY TREATMENT" decision procedure — **generated =
atmosphere/abstract, scraped = show a real named thing; never GENERATE a stand-in for a real thing**).
Fetch + place them like this (SKILL.md step 4c):
```
meta = imagefetch.fetch("Tokyo rail network map", "images/doc/railmap_raw.png", prefer="map")  # -> attrib dict or None
imagefetch.duotone("images/doc/railmap_raw.png", "images/doc/railmap.png",           # treat to match a styled deck
                   shadow=<--fg rgb>, mid=<--accent rgb>, highlight=<--bg rgb>)       # (skip for a photo-real style)
line = imagefetch.attribution_line(meta)   # "Artist · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons"
```
```html
<body>
  <img class="bg-photo" src="file:///ABS/OUT/images/doc/railmap.png" alt="">
  <div class="scrim" style="background:linear-gradient(...var(--fg)...)"></div>   <!-- darken for legible text -->
  <div class="stage"><!-- the beat's real text/number over the image --></div>
  <div class="credit">Artist · CC BY 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons</div>   <!-- ⚠ SIBLING of .stage, NOT inside it -->
</body>
```
- **`.credit` is REQUIRED** for a CC-BY image (attribution), and MUST be a **direct child of `<body>`**,
  a sibling of `.stage` — NOT inside `.stage`. It's `position:absolute` in the lower corner; placed inside
  `.stage`, `keyframe_qa`'s overflow probe (which measures `.stage *`) counts it as content spilling past
  the canvas and FAILS the page. On a dark scrimmed photo, set `style="color:color-mix(in srgb,var(--bg) 80%,transparent)"`.
- **Fetch can miss** — `imagefetch.fetch` returns `None` when nothing license-clean matched the query;
  fall back to an `atmosphere` texture (mood beat) or `none` (drop the image), never a blank page.
- Numbers/claims still live in the page TEXT — the image shows the subject, the text asserts the fact
  (`critic-content` R1e: the fetched subject must match the beat; the credit must be present).

## AI cover + per-page backgrounds ("look A" — the not-flat option)
When the user picks AI backgrounds, generate a SMALL, coherent set (not one busy image per page —
that fights the content) and place them faithfully:
- **🔑 Make it about THE VIDEO'S TOPIC, not generic decoration.** "Generic broll" bounds the
  *specifics* (no fabricated logos/text/named things) — it does NOT mean topic-neutral. Every cover
  and texture must visually EVOKE THE SUBJECT of this video, derived from the comprehension brief:
  a video about neural nets → abstract node/layer imagery; about coffee sourcing → beans/terraces;
  about slide-design → blank slide panels & layout grids. **Litmus test:** hide the text — could a
  viewer still tell what the video is about? If not, the image is decoration, not broll — rewrite
  the motif. A pretty-but-unrelated "editorial paper texture / soft gradient" is a MISS.
- **Cover (hero):** a full-bleed `.bg-photo` + graded `.scrim` on the opener (scene 1) and, mirrored,
  the closer — an atmospheric, **on-topic** broll whose motif comes from the subject (e.g. for a talk
  ON DATA PIPELINES: "abstract flowing conduits and nodes of light, warm <accent>/<accent2> palette,
  soft depth, minimal, no text, no logos"). Blank/abstract surfaces keep it faithful; the SUBJECT
  keeps it relevant. Ken-Burns is fine on the hero.
- **Content pages are NOT flat in the AI look.** EVERY content page carries a reused low-opacity topic
  texture: 2–3 textures **rotated** behind the pages as `.bg-soft` (**opacity ~.12, cap .14**) +
  `.bg-soft-tint`, so every page reads "not flat" while text stays legible on `.card.glass`. The
  design-director emits `meta.soft_texture_prompts` (2–3 on-topic broll prompts); `imagegen`
  synthesizes them into `meta.soft_textures`, which the director rotates by scene index. The opener/
  closer stay image-forward (`.bg-photo`, ~.34–.46). **`validate.py` warns** an AI-look content page
  that is flat (no `.bg-soft`), a `.bg-soft` over ~.20 opacity, a `.bg-soft` with no `.bg-soft-tint`,
  or a bespoke per-page `.bg-soft` src outside `meta.soft_textures`.
  Reuse the set; don't generate 12 unique busy images. Keep the textures on-topic too
  (a faint motif of the subject), just quieter than the cover. These reused soft textures are deck-level
  atmosphere, so **only the TOPIC litmus applies** (not the per-beat one that image-forward media gets —
  `critic-content` R1e exempts them deliberately).
- **Generate:** `imagegen._generate_codex(prompt, out_path)` (Codex, no key) or
  `imagegen.generate(prompt, out_path, key)` (OpenAI key); cache under `.assets/`. Prompts are generic
  **broll** — no logos, faces, named things, or in-image text — AND topically evocative of the video's
  subject; a background NEVER carries a fact, but it should never look like it belongs to a different video.

## Soft AI backgrounds + glass cards (depth without clutter)
To give a designed deck more depth, place a **generic, atmospheric AI image** (a `broll` —
no logos/text/specific subjects) BEHIND the content at low opacity, and put the real content in
**translucent "glass" cards** so the backdrop reads *through* the blocks instead of being fully
covered. Keep it subtle — the image adds atmosphere, the text still carries every fact.

- **Per-page soft backdrop:** first child of `<body>`, then a tint for palette cohesion:
  ```html
  <img class="bg-soft" src="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/.assets/<hash>.png" alt="" style="opacity:.14">
  <div class="bg-soft-tint"></div>
  ```
  Tune `opacity` inline: **content/middle pages ~.12 (cap .14)** — validate warns above ~.20; the
  **atmospheric opener & closer ends ~.34–.46** (more image-forward, since those beats are sparse).
  Two or three reused textures across the content pages keep it cohesive and cheap — you do NOT need a
  distinct image per page (rotate `meta.soft_textures` by scene index).
- **Glass cards:** add `glass` to any `.card` so the backdrop shows through:
  `<div class="card glass">…</div>`. The translucency is an alpha fill (renders under the
  `--disable-gpu` screenshot path); the `backdrop-filter` blur is a bonus that may be ignored.
- **Faithfulness + topicality:** the soft image is decorative `broll` only — generic/atmospheric,
  never a specific vehicle/person/logo and never embedded text or numbers (facts stay in the card
  text) — AND its motif must still evoke the VIDEO'S TOPIC (generic bounds the specifics, not the
  subject). A backdrop that could sit behind any deck is a miss; tie the motif to the subject.
- **Generate the images** with `imagegen` (the same provider as the rest of the tier): Codex
  (`imagegen._generate_codex(prompt, out_path)`, no key) when the `codex` CLI is present, else the
  OpenAI key path (`imagegen.generate(prompt, out_path, key)`); reference the cached file by
  `file://`. Per-page AI imagery is **opt-in** (it costs time/credits) — present the prompts and
  get sign-off before generating, exactly like the non-HTML gpt-image tier.

### Living backdrop (make it breathe, deterministically)
A still backdrop can feel flat; a **GIF/video backdrop is wrong** — our renderer freshly loads each
frame at `?p=`, so a GIF freezes at frame 0 (no motion) or, in a persistent page, jitters on wall-clock
time (non-deterministic, breaks the clip cache + A/V gate). The right way to add life is a slow,
**seek-frozen** motion driven by our own progress. Three tools, in order of subtlety:

- **`.bg-live` / `.bg-drift`** — a very slow Ken-Burns push (or lateral parallax) on a **full-bleed**
  `.bg-soft`/`.bg-photo`. Add the class next to the backdrop: `<img class="bg-soft bg-live" …>`. These
  are **AMBIENT**: `seek.js` drives them by PROGRESS (0→1 over the whole scene) and leaves them OUT of
  the reveal-stagger envelope, so the backdrop spans the full scene AND adding it can **never** shift
  when a reveal fires (unlike the classic `.kenburns`, whose duration *does* enter the envelope — that's
  why `.bg-live` is the preferred living primitive for a content page). Keep it a **whisper**: at
  `.bg-soft`'s ~.12 (cap .14) opacity a ~6% push (`.bg-live`) or a ~3% lateral parallax (`.bg-drift`) is felt,
  not seen. **One** living motion per page; **full-bleed only** — never on a `.split` side image or a
  card (those stay still next to revealing text).
- **`.kenburns`** — the classic hero push, still correct on a full-bleed cover `.bg-photo` (see
  "Cover" above). Reserved for heroes; disabled inside `.split`.
- **`.reveal-wipe`** — a directional foreground reveal (clip-path mask sweep) for an element whose
  meaning is *filling/directional* (`.rule`, `.segbar`, a `.media` panel). This is motion *in the
  content*, not the backdrop — the **foreground alternative** in the same living-motion family: pick
  ONE per page (a breathing backdrop OR a wiping panel), not both.

Under **reduced motion** the backdrops (and the `.kenburns` push) go static, and `.reveal-wipe` drops
its directional sweep to reveal via a plain opacity fade instead; all pass `keyframe_qa` (full-bleed
ambients don't trip the overflow probe). Do not stack them — one moving thing at a time. `validate.py`
warns on >1 living backdrop or a `.bg-live`/`.bg-drift` on a non-full-bleed element (the raw
`[data-ambient]` hook is an advanced escape hatch — not full-bleed-linted, so you own its placement).

**Render note:** an ambient page is captured **every frame** (the backdrop moves continuously, so the
frame-copy hold optimization is disabled for it) — affordable because living backdrops are rare
(hero/hold beats). Pair it with the **edge-tts cued path**: reveals settle at their cue and then hold
while the backdrop keeps breathing. In the cue-less paced fallback there's only one progress clock, so
the reveals spread across the whole scene alongside the backdrop — a calm, correct look for a sparse
hero/closer, but the reason a living backdrop belongs on sparse beats, not dense content pages.

## SVG icons (category marks, used with restraint) — see `references/icons.md`
Inline-SVG line icons (one coherent Lucide family, themeable via `currentColor`) can mark a row of
**category / feature cards** or flag status. Use the `.icon-tile` / `.icon-badge` / `.icon` classes
(in `motifs.css`) and paste a glyph from `references/icons.md`. Discipline (enforced by `critic-content`):
an icon must do a JOB (answer *what is this / what does it do / why care*) — never decoration; ONE
family; **semantic fit**; color-code a category row by setting `color:` per tile; keep the text label;
≤ the title size; and **no icon on an evidence/stat beat** (a `chart`/number/figure is the focal
point). A few, consistent, purposeful — not one on every page.

## Theming (topic-fitting color)
Link the stylesheets in THIS order: `base.css` → **`theme.css`** → `motifs.css`. `theme.css` is
written by `scripts/theme.py <out_dir>` (it samples `frames/` for a curated light/dark palette, or
takes `--mode/--accent/--bg` for a topic palette) and overrides the `:root` vars. **Author pages
with the semantic vars only** — `var(--bg) var(--surface) var(--fg) var(--muted) var(--accent)
var(--accent2) var(--rule) var(--scrim) var(--on-accent)` (older `var(--blue)/var(--orange)` still
alias to the accents). Never hardcode a hex in a page — that's how a page goes off-theme.

**Film grain (automatic).** `theme.py` emits `--grain-amount` per style, and `motifs.css` paints a
fixed-seed feTurbulence grain over the whole frame via `body::after` — so a *printed/filmic* style
(risograph, manga, watercolor, terminal, noir, cartographic) gets a subtle filmic surface on the FREE
tier with zero author effort, while clean styles (swiss, glass, cyberpunk, …) stay crisp at `0`. You
don't add anything. On a data-heavy page where the noise fights a chart/table, add `class="no-grain"`
to that page's `<body>` to switch it off for that scene only.

## Illustrated content page (image + Ken-Burns)
A content beat with `media` becomes a two-column `.split` page: text on one side, an image panel on
the other. The side image is held **STATIC** — a zooming image next to revealing bullets is
distracting (and steps with the cue capture). Ken-Burns is reserved for full-bleed hero `.bg-photo`
backdrops; inside a `.split` it's disabled by `.split .media img{animation:none}`.
```html
<div class="split">
  <div><div class="kicker reveal">SECTION</div>
    <div class="title reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.1s">Headline</div>
    <div class="grid" style="margin-top:28px;gap:22px">
      <div class="row reveal-up" style="animation-delay:.3s"><span class="dot"></span><span class="label">Point</span></div>
    </div></div>
  <div class="media"><img class="kenburns" src="file:///ABS/OUT_DIR/.assets/<hash>.png" alt=""></div>
</div>
```
The `src` is the storyboard's `slide.image` value (imagegen caches under `.assets/<hash>.png`),
referenced as `file://<out_dir>/<slide.image>`. Do NOT use a literal `assets/scene_NN.png` path.
The image is a generic atmospheric **broll** (generated via `imagegen`); the facts stay as text.
Only CSS animation (`.kenburns` + reveals) — no JS-timed motion, no network assets — so `seek.js`
captures it deterministically.

## Typographic roles (use the named classes — never a raw font-size)
`.stat` = a single data value · `.title` = the primary claim · `.sub` = supporting context (always
`--muted`) · `.kicker` = a category label (mono, accent-coloured) · `.note` = secondary annotation. Keep
the hierarchy contract: `.title`/`.sub` ≥ 2.5×, `.title`/`.note` ≥ 3×. (`var(--blue)`/`var(--orange)`
are semantic *accent aliases*, not hardcoded colours — using them is fine; a literal `#rrggbb` is not.)
Body/running text (`.sub`, `.note`, long paragraphs) is **LEFT-ALIGNED** — a centered multi-line
paragraph doesn't scan (`keyframe_qa` flags it); centering is for display elements (titles,
pull-quotes, stats) and centered diagram archetypes only.

## Layout diversity — no samey deck (enforced)
Across the deck's `html` scenes, **no single form family may exceed ~45%**. A deck that is card/row
grids top to bottom reads as auto-generated — the exact "AI slop" this tier exists to avoid. If you're
reaching for a card grid a third time, STOP and re-read the form-selection table above: the content
almost always wants a `.flow` / `.scorecard` / `.quadrant` / `.timeline` / `.hubspoke` / `.segbar`
instead. `validate.py` counts the families and warns when one dominates; `design-critic` (D1) fails it.

## Decodability rule — every on-frame element must telegraph its role (REQUIRED)
A viewer gets each frame for only a few seconds. **Every visible element must pass a 1-second test:
a first-time viewer can name what it is and why it's there.** Existence-for-composition is NOT enough —
an element that "balances the layout" but can't be decoded reads as a rendering bug, not design.
Concretely:
- **No empty/unlabeled furniture.** An empty box, a bare pill, an unexplained badge = a MYSTERY the
  viewer stops to puzzle over. If a counterweight is needed, use an element that carries meaning
  (a labeled secondary object, a captioned chip, a titled panel) — or trust the void (deliberate
  whitespace beats mysterious filler; see the off-center bands).
- **Chrome must be idiomatic.** Register furniture (rulers, guides, selection handles, zoom badges)
  is allowed ONLY when it reproduces an idiom the audience already knows at a glance; if a furniture
  piece needs relabeling to dodge a lint (e.g. "100%"→"1:1"), that's a sign to REMOVE it, not rename
  it — never sacrifice human legibility to satisfy a machine check.
- **Abstract placeholders live INSIDE labeled objects.** Ghost text-lines/blocks are fine as the
  *content* of a named thing ("taste.md · 口味档案" + ghost lines = a file); free-floating they're noise.
The design-critic (D11) flags any element it cannot assign a decodable role from the pixels alone.
**Mechanical hooks:** `keyframe_qa` advises on any *empty bordered box with no text and no role* —
an element whose idiom is genuinely glance-readable (a selection frame, a window outline) declares it
with **`data-role="…"`** (e.g. `data-role="selection-frame"`), which is both the opt-out AND
self-documentation. Text that is *interface idiom, not a content claim* (a zoom badge's "100%",
window-chrome labels) is marked **`data-ui`** on the leaf element — `validate.py` then excludes it
from the figure-traceability scan, so there is NEVER a reason to mutate chrome text to silence a lint.

## Alignment & order discipline (the canvas is a grid — behave like one)
Loose scatter reads as sloppiness, not style — deliberate asymmetry needs deliberate ALIGNMENT:
- **Snap to a coarse grid.** Hand-placed absolute positions align to ~20px steps; elements that share
  a row/column share the EXACT same x/y. Edges are either exactly aligned or clearly different —
  never off by a hair (`keyframe_qa` advises on sibling edges off by 5–22px, the "almost aligned" smell).
- **Grids are equal-height.** Cards in one grid get one fixed height (interior extras pinned with
  `margin-top:auto`), so bottoms form a line, not a rag.
- **Bands span and baseline-align.** A row of objects (artboards, chips, tiles) spans the full content
  width (`justify-content:space-between`) with bottoms on one baseline — not a cluster of postage
  stamps floating in a corner — and sits under a rule/caption that names the band.
- **Kill dead zones.** After composing, squint at the four quadrants: a large empty corner that isn't
  DELIBERATE whitespace (an off-center void, air over a hero) is a composition hole — rebalance with
  meaning-carrying elements, never with mystery filler (see the Decodability rule above).

## Composition helpers (pair with the forms above)
- **`.card`** — a panel with depth (`--surface` + shadow + hairline); group related rows. **`.card.glass`** over a soft backdrop.
- **`.dash`** (3-up) / **`.grid-asym`** (2fr 1fr) — dashboard + asymmetric layouts; break the centred-column monotony.
- **`.stage.frame-left` / `.frame-right` / `.thirds`** — OFF-CENTER bands: park the whole content column in ONE
  horizontal third and leave a DELIBERATE void on the other side (real negative space, NOT a 2fr/1fr card
  split). The reference class's most reliable "art-directed" silhouette — reads the same in 16:9 and 9:16,
  needs no data/imagery, and pairs beautifully with a `.bg-photo`/`.bg-soft`/`.bg-motif` breathing in the
  void. Add the class to the `<div class="stage …">` itself. `validate.py` credits it as genuine asymmetry
  (a `frame-left` hero counts toward the ≥⅓ off-center quota). Reach for it on a hook/hero/divider beat.
- **`.defocus`** — on a comparison, add to the NON-focal side for depth-of-field (subtle blur, not flat dim).
- **`.accent-fill`** — on `<body>` of a section-divider beat: full-bleed accent background, `--on-accent` text.
- **`.reveal-pop`** — spring overshoot for a hero `.stat`/`.num`. **`.reveal-up-sm`** — shorter rise for dense sub-items.
- **`.reveal-wipe`** — a left-to-right mask reveal (clip-path). ONLY for elements whose meaning is
  filling/directional — `.rule`, `.segbar`, `.meter .fill`, a `.media` image panel (the FILLS/DRAWS
  verbs); never on text rows/cards (text enters by opacity/rise). One direction deck-wide, at most
  1–2 uses per video — an option, not a default.
- **`.chrome`** — a mono SECTION-LABEL rail (direct child of `<body>`); reuse the section/topic name across beats as a quiet editorial through-line. **NOT a page number / progress bar / counter** (that's the banned player-chrome — a video has nothing to navigate). ⚠️ **Use it ONLY when `meta.captions:false`:** the rail sits at `bottom:56px`, inside the burned caption band (bottom ~8% of the canvas) — with captions ON (the default) they collide, text under text. `validate.py` warns on this; the page's top kicker already labels the section, so with captions just drop `.chrome`.

## Component motion — re-enact the data (opt-in, seek-safe)
Beyond the entrance reveals, a small vocabulary animates the ENCODING inside a data archetype so the
motion RE-ENACTS the fact. Each is paused (seek.js freezes it at `?p=`), deterministic, its final frame
= the static render, and reduced-motion collapses it to the end-state. Use ONE per component, carry
`data-cue-index` to fire on the spoken word, never over a living backdrop. All OPT-IN — omit and the
component is exactly as today.
- **`.grow-w` / `.grow-h`** — a solid fill GROWS from the baseline to its authored size (magnitude).
  For `.meter .fill` / `.segbar .seg` / `.bullet .val` / a solid `.bar`; a LABELLED bar distorts under
  scale, so fade its label with `.reveal` or sweep it with `.reveal-wipe` instead. `.grow-h` (origin
  bottom) for a vertical `.waterfall .wbar`.
- **`.rail-fill`** — a `.stepper`/`.timeline` rail segment FILLS forward toward the node it leads into
  (progress). Author the rail as a real child element; give each segment the cue of the step it leads to.
- **`.draw-down`** — a vertical connector EXTENDS from source toward destination (flow direction; the
  non-SVG cousin of `.draw`). Borrows the destination block's `data-cue-index`.
- **`.settle`** — the focal cell/row/node SETTLES in LAST from just-below full size (never `scale(0)`),
  paired with its static `.on` ring. "This is the one."
- **`.cross-dim`** — the NON-focal side of a comparison DIMS (to .42, still legible) as the focal side is
  named. Pairs with `.defocus` / `rtable tr.win` / `.cell.on`.
- **`.count-up`** — a pure-CSS COUNT for a value that genuinely accumulates (a total/score). Author
  `<span class="count-up num" style="--count-to:87"></span>` (+ a sibling `.unit` for %/×). Never a
  static label. (Chrome `@property`; modern headless supports it.)
- **`.gauge.sweep`** — the `.gauge` arc SWEEPS to its `--p` fraction (radial magnitude). Add `.sweep`
  to a `.gauge`; the hole/value stay put.

## Reveal timing — points must NOT lead the voice (important)
The most common defect is **content appearing well before the narration reaches it**. Avoid it:
- **Multi-point content pages MUST be audio-synced with `data-cue`** (see "Audio-synced reveals"
  below) — the precise *and* efficient path: each point reveals exactly when its spoken anchor is
  heard, and the renderer only screenshots around each cue. This is the default for any page with
  ≥2 content points; the content-planner emits a per-beat `cue` array to support it.
- **If a page is NOT cued, leave `anim_seconds` UNSET** on content pages — the renderer defaults it to
  spread the reveals across ~70% of the scene (tracking the speaking pace) instead of cramming them into
  the first second. Set `anim_seconds` explicitly only for heroes/title pages (~1.2–1.5s) or to override.
  Do NOT set a small `anim_seconds` (2–3s) on a long (10s+) content page — every point flashes in early
  and the rest of the scene is static. **`validate.py` warns** when an uncued multi-point page has an
  `anim_seconds` < half the scene; **`critic-content` (R2) also flags reveals that lead the audio.**

## Stagger cadence (seek-safe)
- **Header chrome** (kicker → rule → title → sub) appears fast: `0s`, `.05s`, `.10s`, `.25s`.
- **Content POINTS appear ONE BY ONE — MUST, not should.** Every component that carries its own
  meaning is its OWN reveal element with its OWN `data-cue-index` (monotonically increasing, `0..N-1`
  contiguous, in spoken order), anchored via `data-cue=` to the phrase that introduces it — so
  components land one at a time and guide the viewer step by step. A reveal wrapper may group ONLY a
  tight visual unit (a number + its unit/▲▼, a "label: value" line-item, an icon + its label — a pure
  descriptor `.label`/`.note`/`.bar`/`.delta`/`.unit` is PART of its number/row, not a separate fact).
  If a wrapper holds ≥2 independently-meaningful **line-items or primary numbers** (≥2 of
  `.stat`/`.num`/`.row`/`.tile`/`.step`/`.block`/`.seg`/`.hs-spoke`), SPLIT them into separate cued
  reveal children. On a cued page **NO reveal element may be uncued
  except header chrome** (`.kicker`/`.rule`/`.title`/`.sub`) — an uncued reveal keeps
  `animation-delay:0` and flashes in at ~0.7s WITH the header, leading the voice. `validate.py` warns
  on uncued reveals, ≥2-facts-per-cue wrappers, and index gaps; `keyframe_qa` advises when a paced
  page's reveals don't stagger across the frozen states; `design-critic` D6 REVISEs an all-at-once page.
- **The FIRST reveal must land at the scene's OPENING — never leave the page BLANK while the voice
  talks.** Header chrome (`.kicker`/`.rule`/`.title`/`.sub`) shows in the ~1.2s head window, so a page
  WITH one is never empty at the start. But a **no-header hero / pull-quote / stat** whose only content
  is anchored to a phrase spoken partway through sits BLANK for seconds while the narration's opening
  plays — which reads as broken. Fix: anchor the FIRST reveal to the narration's **opening phrase** (the
  hero's framing line or kicker appears as the voice begins, the big number then lands on ITS phrase),
  or give the page an uncued `.kicker`/`.title`. `validate.py` warns when a no-header cued page's first
  reveal is anchored past ~15% of the narration.
- **CONNECTORS reveal WITH their destination block — never before, never static.** An `.arrow`/
  `.hs-connect` gets `reveal` (a plain fade, NOT `.reveal-up`, so a directional glyph doesn't slide)
  + `data-cue-index` = its DESTINATION block's index (the LATER of the two nodes it joins; for
  `.hs-connect`, the hub's). It carries **no `data-cue=`** of its own — it borrows the destination's
  cue slot via `seek.js`, so nothing new is scraped and the render is unchanged. A static connector
  among cued blocks paints from frame 0, before the blocks — **`validate.py` errors on it.** (The
  single `.timeline::before` rail is a CSS backdrop, not a per-step connector, so it stays static.)
  - **Bespoke SVG lines/arcs/chevrons in a diagram follow the SAME rule — mark them `.connector`.** A
    hand-drawn `<path>`/`<polyline>` that connects or points between cued nodes must (a) carry a
    reveal/`.draw` animation + `data-cue-index` = the cue of the line it belongs to (borrow, no
    `data-cue=` of its own), so it draws/fades WITH that line, and (b) carry the **`.connector`** class
    so `validate.py` treats it as a borrowing connector (exempt from the duplicate/uncued accounting),
    not a stray point. A raw static `<polyline>` has NO animation, so `seek.js` never touches it and it
    paints at frame 0 — the "arrow appears too early" bug. **A DIRECTIONAL arrowhead must sit ON the
    line's centerline and point along its tangent** — for an SVG arc, put the chevron TIP on the exact
    path point (compute it from the arc's own geometry) and splay the wings symmetric to the tangent, so
    the arrow follows the curve instead of floating beside it. Give each drawn segment the cue of the
    beat it's SPOKEN at (a two-arc loop: arc-A on the cue that describes A→B, arc-B on the cue for B→A),
    never a blanket single cue that makes half the diagram lead the narration.
- **Equal-height cards:** rows of cards (`.dash`) are equal height by design (`align-items:stretch`); do
  not set per-card heights. If one card's text is much longer, shorten it or move it to its own beat.
- **Audio-synced cues override stagger:** when audio-synced cues are active (edge-tts + `data-cue`
  attributes), `seek.js` overrides each cued point's delay with its resolved cue time from
  `audio/NN.words.json`; your stagger `animation-delay` values on cued points are ignored.

## One-concept rule + whitespace floor
ONE primary per page (a stat OR a list OR a chart — not two stacked). Content must not fill more than
~60% of the canvas; if a row grid overflows below 960px, SPLIT the beat — never shrink `.stage` padding below 80px.

## 9:16 vertical pages (1080×1920) — LINK `vertical.css`, don't hand-crop
The design system is 1920×1080; a 9:16 deck (`meta.aspect:"9:16"`) just links the **shipped canonical
override `assets/html/vertical.css` LAST** (base.css → theme.css → motifs.css → **vertical.css**). It
restacks EVERY archetype to a 1080 column, top-anchors the stage, applies the phone-first type scale,
**forces `.flow`/`.stepper` connectors DOWN** (so a rotated `↓`→`←` bug is impossible), and rescales the
width-bound (`.code`/`.eqn`/`.rtable`) + fixed-height (`.quadrant`/`.venn`/`.rings`/`.waterfall`/`.gauge`)
forms so they fill the tall column. A per-page `<style>` is then only for a genuine EXCEPTION, not the
baseline. What it already handles (so you don't re-author it):
- **Canvas + backdrops:** `html,body`+`.stage` → 1080×1920 top-anchored; `.bg-photo`/`.bg-soft` are now
  aspect-correct by default (motifs.css sizes them 100%); on a cover hero add `class="scrim vert"` for the
  vertical gradient (dark at top).
- **Top-anchored composition** (NOT the landscape vertical-centering): content opens at ONE
  consistent line ~160px from the top (`.stage{padding:160px 84px 320px;justify-content:flex-start}`)
  and the caption band owns the bottom ~270px — don't center content into it.
- **FILL the column — the cardinal 9:16 rule.** Landscape content ported 1:1 fills ~40% of the
  tall canvas and reads as a mistake. Target: content spans **≥70% of the zone between the top
  line and the caption band** (~y160–1600). Measure it, don't eyeball it — `keyframe_qa.py` reports each page's fill% on a 9:16 deck and
  advises below 60% (heroes with a full-bleed `.bg-photo` exempt); tune until every page clears.
  Two levers: (a) **phone-first type scale** — title ~92px, labels ~44px, sub ~42px, notes ~32px,
  blocks ~250px min-height, segbar ~120px, icon tiles ~88px (the 64–70px "desktop" scale is what
  leaves the dead zone); (b) **distribute along the height** — tall row gaps (~34px), padded
  timeline rows (~22px), and on a SPARSE beat drop a LARGE motif/visual into the lower zone
  (~y1000–1400) instead of a small corner stamp, so the column carries two visual centers.
- **Restack, don't shrink:** `.split`/`.blocks`/multi-column `.grid` → ONE column; the horizontal
  `.timeline` → a **vertical rail** (`flex-direction:column`, rail on the left, node rows beside it);
  `.hs-spokes` gets `width:calc(50% - gap/2)` so it wraps a CLEAN 2×2 (auto widths wrap 1-1-2 at
  phone scale). A squeezed landscape layout reads as a crop, not a design.
- **Vertical `.flow`/`.stepper` connectors point DOWN, not sideways.** When a horizontal flow stacks
  into a column, its `.arrow`/rail must read top→bottom. Author the glyph as **`↓`** (`&#8595;`), and in
  the 9:16 override **do NOT `transform:rotate(90deg)` an authored `↓`** — that yields a sideways `←`
  (a shipped bug). The robust form forces it regardless of the authored glyph:
  `.flow .arrow{transform:none;font-size:0}  .flow .arrow::after{content:"\2193";font-size:52px;color:var(--rule)}`.
- **Research / technical forms — the WIDTH-bound ones need real care in a 1080 column** (they're sized
  for a 1920 row): a `.code` block (`algorithm_build`) must drop to **≤ ~40-char lines** (validate's
  vertical lint enforces this) and a smaller font (~30px) — split or wrap a long line, don't let it
  overflow; a `.eqn` (`equation_build`) shrinks from ~100px to ~64–72px and may need the equation broken
  across two lines; a `.rtable` (`results_table`) drops to ≤3 columns or restacks each row as a labeled
  card. `keyframe_qa --vertical` FAILS any of these that overflow the column, so **re-check every
  technical page after switching aspect** — the naive 16:9 sizing overflows.
- **Motif clearance:** a corner motif needs clear air — ≥80px from any text. On a page with a
  CENTERED / full-width header the top corners aren't free: move the motif to the lower zone
  (where it also helps fill) or drop it. Text stacks need real spacing too (~36–44px between a
  title and its sub-lines at phone scale) — tight stacks above a large void read as a mistake.
- **Keep long unbreakable tokens OUT of the narration** (filenames, URLs, long code): the caption
  column is narrow and `build_yourdeck.py` can't wrap — say "its build script" and show the
  filename ON the page instead.
- **Captions are auto-sized off the narrow dimension** (`min(W,H)*0.045` ≈ 48px in both aspects) —
  the renderer handles it; still re-run `validate.py` after switching aspect (wraps/widows differ)
  and `keyframe_qa.py` (it measures the 1080×1920 DOM and renders aspect-correct contact sheets).

## Anti-slop checklist (do NOT)
emoji in titles · full-screen purple/pink/blue gradient-mesh backgrounds · circle+left-border accent
cards (use `.card`/`.row`) · SVG depicting realistic scenes/figures · decorative bottom progress bars /
timecodes / chapter counters (player-chrome) · hardcoded hex (use semantic vars) · network/CDN links.

## Pre-render checklist
absolute `file://` paths (files exist) · no `<link href="http…">` · base.css → theme.css → motifs.css
linked · no content overflow below 960px · semantic vars only · all `.reveal*`/`.kenburns` keep
`animation-play-state:paused` · no leftover debug overlays · no `.chrome` when captions are on —
then run `python scripts/keyframe_qa.py <out_dir>`: it screenshots every page at 5 reveal states
into `_keyframes/` and mechanically verifies the blank/overflow items above (eyeball `all.png` for
tofu / off-theme / mistimed reveals).

## Audio-synced reveals (points appear when spoken)
On a multi-point page, tag each point's reveal element with `data-cue-index="0|1|2…"` (in SPOKEN
order) and `data-cue="<the spoken anchor phrase>"` — the word/phrase in the narration that introduces
that point (usually the point's keyword; set it to a different phrase only when the visible label is
not spoken verbatim). Example:
```html
<div class="row reveal-up-sm" data-cue-index="0" data-cue="Dujiangyan"> … </div>
<div class="row reveal-up-sm" data-cue-index="1" data-cue="Leshan"> … </div>
```
When edge-tts word timings exist (`audio/NN.words.json`), `render_html` reveals each point exactly when
its anchor is spoken (across the whole scene). With no word timings (macOS `say`, or a missing anchor)
it falls back to the paced `anim_seconds` stagger. Heroes/title pages don't use `data-cue`. The anchor
must be a phrase actually present in that scene's narration.

> ⚠️ **Cued pages capture only the header window + cue bursts.** On a cued page, `render_html`
> shoots fresh frames during the initial header window (~1.2s) and around each cue, and HOLDS
> (copies) elsewhere. So a NON-cued element with a long animation freezes partway: `.float` (3s)
> and `.draw` (1.4s) won't finish. On a cued page, keep non-cued decorative motion short
> (≤ ~1.2s) or give those elements a `data-cue` so they're captured. Plain `.reveal*` header
> chrome is fine (it settles by ~1s).
